ARABIC — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #5
====

GRADE: Grade 10
SUBJECT: ARABIC
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Listening Comprehension, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Listening Comprehension.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening Comprehension.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Listening Comprehension.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Listening Comprehension.

2. When practising Reading for Information, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Reading for Information.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading for Information.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Reading for Information.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Reading for Information.

3. When practising Listening for Gist, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Listening for Gist.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Listening for Gist.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for Gist.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Listening for Gist.

4. In ARABIC, the best classroom habit is: (1 mark)
   A. Only memorise without using the language
   B. Mix random languages with no purpose
   C. Avoid speaking to classmates
   D. Practise listening, speaking, reading, and writing every day

5. When practising Extensive Reading: Library skills, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Extensive Reading: Library skills.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Extensive Reading: Library skills.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Extensive Reading: Library skills.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Extensive Reading: Library skills.

6. When practising Reading for Comprehension, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Reading for Comprehension.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Reading for Comprehension.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading for Comprehension.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Reading for Comprehension.

7. When practising Speaking Fluency, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Speaking Fluency.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Speaking Fluency.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Speaking Fluency.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Speaking Fluency.

8. When practising Selective Listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Selective Listening.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Selective Listening.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Selective Listening.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Selective Listening.

9. When practising Intensive Reading: Poetry, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Intensive Reading: Poetry.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Intensive Reading: Poetry.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Intensive Reading: Poetry.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Intensive Reading: Poetry.

10. When practising Reading Fluency, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading Fluency.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Reading Fluency.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Reading Fluency.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Reading Fluency.

11. When practising Attentive Listening ● Scanning ● Vocabulary Building ● Extracting information, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Attentive Listening ● Scanning ● Vocabulary Building ● Extracting information.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Attentive Listening ● Scanning ● Vocabulary Building ● Extracting information.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Attentive Listening ● Scanning ● Vocabulary Building ● Extracting information.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Attentive Listening ● Scanning ● Vocabulary Building ● Extracting information.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
12. In three clear sentences, explain Paragraph Writing: Sequencing Ideas and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

13. In three clear sentences, explain Descriptive Writing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Creative Writing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Functional Writing: Informal letters and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Word class: Nouns and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

17. In three clear sentences, explain Word classes: Pronouns and Conjunctions and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Word class: Pronouns and Articles and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain Word classes and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

20. In three clear sentences, explain Word class: Verbs and Tenses and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

21. In three clear sentences, explain Sentence patterns and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
